text:
kate_support: customer report — Safari on iOS 16.4: SSE stream from our /v1/stream endpoint sends a first partial event then connection drops. They see a 200 followed immediately by a 304 from the CDN and client stops receiving further chunks. repro steps and headers below.

matt_cdn: can you paste the exact request headers and whether they're going through Cloudflare or Fastly? 304 sounds like edge cache revalidation. :thinking_face:

kate_support: they're on Cloudflare managed site, sending Authorization: Bearer <token>. Here are the minimal repro steps they gave: 
1) open page in Safari iOS
2) new EventSource('/v1/stream?session=abc', { withCredentials: true })
3) stream yields one event, then stalls.

kate_support: they provided the observed network trace (copied):
```
Request: GET /v1/stream?session=abc HTTP/2
Host: api.redwood.example
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer X
Cookie: session=foo

Response 1: HTTP/2 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Encoding: gzip
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Vary: Cookie, Authorization

(body chunk - first event delivered)

Edge revalidate:
Response 2: HTTP/2 304 Not Modified
Date: ...

(connection closes on client)
```

oliver_runtime: ugh. Safari + gzip + chunked + a 304 mid-stream is a known trigger for it to treat stream as finished. Safari apparently doesn't tolerate a 304 after initial partial body on SSE. We should reproduce with curl and with a minimal HTML EventSource.

sarah_engineering: quick triage checklist: 
- verify server never returns Content-Length for event-stream (shouldn't)
- ensure CDN is not returning 304 for requests with Authorization/Cookie (edge should bypass cache or vary correctly)
- check if gzip is being applied at edge (Edge should not re-encode chunking mid-stream)

matt_cdn: confirmed Cloudflare can revalidate and hit origin with conditional ETag if configured under certain cache rules even when Authorization present if rules allow. The Vary: Authorization + Cookie is weird for SSE. Edge might store 0-length object then return 304. I can ask them to temporarily disable cache for /v1/stream route.

kate_support: customer is OK to test disabling cache. they're asking if we have a recommended workaround so production apps don't break for Safari users.

oliver_runtime: workaround options: 
- ensure CDN cache-control: no-store or Cache-Control: private, no-transform, no-cache (force pass-through), and remove ETag/Vary that causes revalidation mid-stream
- avoid Content-Encoding: gzip at the edge for chunked SSE responses (deliver uncompressed chunked streams)
- provide a polling or websocket fallback for Safari (polyfill that uses fetch + ReadableStream is common)

sarah_engineering: also try adding a keepalive comment every ~15s from server: `: keepalive\n\n` (SSE comment) so Safari doesn't consider the connection idle. But this doesn't fix a 304 blowup.

matt_cdn: I pushed a quick rule to the customer's Cloudflare zone to bypass cache for `path:/v1/stream*` and disabled ETag. They repro again and confirm it stays open longer but still sees occasional chunk truncation when gzip is on.

kate_support: customer reports "longer, but still stops sometimes after 60-90s".

oliver_runtime: next step: we should reproduce using a Cloudflare worker or a simple nginx origin forwarding with identical headers so we can iterate. I'll spin up an env and run wkhtml or iOS simulator.

sarah_engineering: can you also capture an HAR from Safari (via macOS proxy or remote debug) and upload? need full TLS handshake and headers.

oliver_runtime: reproducer steps I'll try: 
- `mkfifo /tmp/pipe; while read; do echo -n "data: $(date)\n\n" > /tmp/pipe; sleep 1; done &`
- `socat -v tcp-listen:8080,reuseaddr,fork file:/tmp/pipe`
- serve headers exactly: Content-Type: text/event-stream; Transfer-Encoding: chunked; Cache-Control: private, no-cache; no Content-Length; Content-Encoding: gzip (optional)

I will test with and without gzip at edge and with Cloudflare bypass.

kate_support: customer asked if we can implement an API-side header change on hosted API for Safari user-agents as a band-aid (disable gzip / add no-transform). Is that feasible?

sarah_engineering: not comfortable doing UA-sniffing long-term but we could expose a `sse_compat` boolean param on the stream endpoint that toggles `Content-Encoding` and adds `Cache-Control: no-store` for those requests. Short term ok if team agrees.

matt_cdn: Agree—exposing a param is safer than UA sniffing. I'll coordinate a Cloudflare rule doc for customers to set bypass.

kate_support: customer accepted: they'll test the `?sse_compat=1` param. They've also attached a short screen recording and HAR. I'll upload the HAR to the ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy 1795557700 completed: feature/sse-compat-flag -> staging

sarah_engineering: i'll pick this up next sprint to add the flag and unit test that headers are uncompressed and cache-bypassed. Oliver pls include integration test that simulates 304 mid-stream and asserts client keeps connection (or that server never returns 304).

oliver_runtime: noted. I'll add an integration probe and a small Safari remote test against staging. Will report back with timeline.

kate_support: thanks all — I'll keep customer updated and mark ticket as "waiting on engineering". :slightly_smiling_face:
